analyses.failure: test_chk_007_rx_overrun — CHK-001 (Python sink checker): "m_axis stalled with tvalid=1 tdata=0x3c after tready=0 got tvalid=1 tdata=0xc3 at edge 322" (sim.log:41-47)
analyses.spec_says: spec/c_uart_Design_Specification.md:36-38: "Data is transferred from the source to the destination only when both tvalid and tready are high, otherwise the bus is stalled." spec:42-44: "If the data word currently in the tdata output register is not read before another word is received, then a single cycle pulse will be emitted from overrun_error and the word is discarded." The spec does not say which word is discarded. rules.json:167 (UA-T1.3-07 statement) reads it as "discards the newly received word". rules.json:300-301 raises the open question "On overrun, is the newly received word discarded while the older word in the tdata register is retained? ... The designer must specify which word is dropped on overrun", and answered_questions is empty (rules.json:304). contract.json:317 (assumption): "The spec quote 'the word is discarded' could be read either way, and the checks follow the approved rule." contract.json:256-258 (CHK-007): "The newly received word is discarded and the pending word is kept ... m_axis_tdata=0x3C at every edge after W1 is presented ... 0xC3 is never transferred."
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/uart_rx.v:120-125: when the stop bit is sampled (bit_cnt==1) and rxd_reg==1, the RTL always runs m_axis_tdata_reg <= data_reg (l.123) and m_axis_tvalid_reg <= 1 (l.124). It only flags overrun_error_reg <= m_axis_tvalid_reg (l.125). Nothing stops the write when a word is already pending (m_axis_tvalid_reg=1, m_axis_tready=0). So at W2's stop-bit sample (edge 322, about t2+153), the pending 0x3C in the output register is replaced by 0xC3 while tvalid stays 1 and tready=0. The old word is the one discarded and the new word is kept. The SVA a_CHK_001 (verif/sva/nnc_chk_axis.sv:25-27) also fired: sim.log:94 "NNC_FAIL CHK-001 @254585000" and sim.log:139 "CHK-001 hits=405 fails=1". This RTL matches the upstream Forencich source that the spec README describes (spec:1).
analyses.test_does: test_c_uart.py:449-486. Sink mode 'off' (tready=0, l.452). Drives W1=0x3C at bp=16 (l.454) and waits for tvalid=1 (l.455). Keeps tready=0 and drives W2=0xC3 (l.458). AxisSink._run (l.173-176) checks every cycle that if the previous sample had tvalid=1 and tready=0, then tvalid=1 and tdata is unchanged. That is CHK-001 as written in contract.json:181 ("the pending word is neither dropped nor overwritten, even if another frame finishes on rxd in the meantime (overrun discards the new word)"). The expected value 0x3C comes from UartRefModel (l.302-304, "new word is discarded (pending word kept)"), which follows the contract assumption at contract.json:317. The test fails at the first cycle the RTL overwrites the data.

candidates.evidence_for: AXI4-Stream stall wording at spec:36-38 ("otherwise the bus is stalled") supports keeping tdata stable while tvalid=1 and tready=0. RTL uart_rx.v:123 changes m_axis_tdata while tvalid=1 and tready=0, so a downstream that samples tdata at its own handshake gets a different word than was presented. Both the independent SVA (nnc_chk_axis.sv:25-26) and the Python checker flag it.
candidates.evidence_against: The overrun sentence (spec:42-44) names "the data word currently in the tdata output register" as the subject, and "the word is discarded" can grammatically refer to that old word, which is exactly what the RTL does (l.123 overwrites, l.125 pulses overrun). The spec is the upstream README of this exact RTL (spec:1), so the overwrite looks like the author's intended behaviour.

candidates.evidence_for: The test and SVA encode one reading (new word discarded), taken from rules.json:167 and contract.json:317, not from an unambiguous spec sentence. If the designer confirms the RTL reading, CHK-001's "even if another frame finishes" clause and the CHK-007 expectations (contract.json:256-258) do not follow from the spec.
candidates.evidence_against: The stimulus is legal (tready=0, a second full frame). The checker matches the CHK-001 behaviour text exactly (test l.173-176, contract.json:181). The AXI stall rule (spec:36-38) independently supports the expectation. Nothing in the test is mis-timed: the fail is at the W2 stop-bit sample, where uart_rx.v:123 executes.

candidates.evidence_for: rules.json:300-301 records this exact unanswered question ("is the newly received word discarded while the older word in the tdata register is retained?"), with answered_questions empty (rules.json:304). contract.json:317 admits "could be read either way". The two spec sentences pull in different directions: the stall rule (spec:36-38) favours the test, and the overrun sentence's subject (spec:42-44) favours the RTL.
candidates.evidence_against: The AXI-Stream stall sentence alone is a fairly direct requirement that a stalled bus does not change. A designer may consider it decisive, which would make this an RTL bug rather than an ambiguity.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec: answer rules.json question UA-T1.3-07 by stating which word is discarded on overrun, and whether the AXI stall rule (spec:36-38) applies to m_axis during overrun. (2) If the answer is 'keep the pending word': fix RTL uart_rx.v:122-125 so tdata/tvalid are only loaded when !m_axis_tvalid_reg || m_axis_tready (e.g. `if (m_axis_tvalid_reg && !m_axis_tready) overrun_error_reg <= 1; else begin m_axis_tdata_reg <= data_reg; m_axis_tvalid_reg <= 1; end`). The existing CHK-001/CHK-007 then stand unchanged. (3) If the answer is 'the old word is overwritten (upstream behaviour)': change the contract and test, not the strength of the check. Change rule UA-T1.3-07's statement and contract.json:181/256-258. CHK-001 then needs an explicit, spec-backed exception for the overrun edge (rx_overrun_error=1 at N+1), and CHK-007's expected data becomes 0xC3 with UartRefModel.rx_good(pending=True) replacing the pending word. Document the deviation from AXI stall semantics in the spec.

analyses.failure: test_chk_008_rx_frame_error — "CHK-008: m_axis_tvalid=0 from bad frame until valid frame at every edge 9..513 got m_axis_tvalid=1 at edge 314 (1 violating edges)" (sim.log:51-59)
analyses.spec_says: spec/c_uart_Design_Specification.md:44-46: "If the receiver does not get a stop bit of the right level, then a single pulse will be emitted from the frame_error output and the received word will be discarded." (rules.json:180, UA-T1.3-08). The spec says nothing about start-bit detection, break or a line held low after a bad stop bit, or when the receiver may look for the next start bit. contract.json:269-270 (CHK-008) adds: the bad stop bit is "held at 0 for a full bit period", and "m_axis_tvalid stays 0 from the bad frame until the valid frame is received".
analyses.rtl_does: Reconstructed from the RTL with tb=9, bp=16, prescale=2. Start detected at edge 11 (uart_rx.v:132-136, prescale_reg=(2<<2)-2=6), start bit confirmed at edge 18 (l.108-111), data bits at 34..146 (l.116-119). The stop bit is sampled at edge 162 with rxd_reg=0, so frame_error pulses (l.127) and 0xA5 is discarded, as the spec requires. Edge 163: bit_cnt=0, so the idle branch (l.130-137) sees rxd_reg still 0 (the stop bit is held low until the falling edge after 169) and starts a NEW reception on level, not on a falling edge. Edge 170: the start-bit check l.109 sees rxd_reg = rxd from edge 169 = 0, so the start is accepted. The line is then idle-high, so 8 data bits of 1 and a good stop give m_axis_tdata=0xFF, tvalid=1 at 170+9*16 = 314 (l.122-124), exactly the reported edge. Supporting coverage: the false-start abort path uart_rx.v:112-114 was never executed (results.json:205-273), COVP-022 'good reception after a frame error' hit=1, and COVP-014 (handshake data all ones) hit 5 (sim.log). These match a phantom 0xFF frame.
analyses.test_does: test_c_uart.py:490-512. Sink 'on'. Sends 0xA5 with stop=0 (l.495). UartLineDriver.send (l.236-244) holds every bit, including the stop 0, for bp=16 cycles and then sets rxd=1 (l.243). It waits 200 cycles, then sends 0x96 (l.498). It checks one frame_error pulse in [mid_stop, frame_end+2bp] (l.503-506), which presumably passed because that assertion comes before the failing one. Then it checks m_axis_tvalid==0 at every edge from tb to tg+(DW+1)*bp (l.507-508; edges 9..513). The expectation comes from contract.json:270, which extends spec 'received word will be discarded' to 'no word at all until the valid frame'. The later check got==[0x96] (l.511-512) would also fail, since 0xFF is handshaken.

candidates.evidence_for: The DUT produces a word (0xFF) that was never transmitted, built from the tail of a bad stop bit plus idle line. Many UARTs require the line to return to mark (1) before detecting a new start bit after a framing error or break. The RTL detects start on level (uart_rx.v:132) right after the frame error and lets it through because the start check at l.109 lands on the last low cycle.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec only requires a frame_error pulse and that "the received word" (0xA5) is discarded, and the RTL does both (l.126-127). No spec sentence defines start-bit detection or post-error resynchronisation. The result depends on a one-cycle boundary: one cycle less of low stop bit and l.109 would see 1 and abort at l.112-114.

candidates.evidence_for: The stimulus holds the stop bit at 0 for exactly one full bit period. Combined with the RTL's half-bit start check, this lands the second start validation exactly on the last low cycle (edge 170 sees rxd from edge 169), a race the spec does not address. The no-tvalid window (l.507) asserts more than the spec sentence (spec:46), which is about the received word only. The phantom frame is a separate reception the spec does not forbid.
candidates.evidence_against: Holding a bad stop bit low for a full bit period is a natural, legal frame-error stimulus, written into contract.json:269. Expecting no spurious word on m_axis is a reasonable reading of 'the received word will be discarded'. Real-world line conditions (break, noise) would hit the same case.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec (spec:44-46) defines only the error pulse and discarding the bad word. It does not say whether the receiver must wait for an idle (1) level after a framing error, or how a start bit is detected (edge or level, sampling point). The contract assumption list (contract.json:312-320) does not cover this either. Whether 0xFF at edge 314 is legal depends entirely on that unstated rule.
candidates.evidence_against: A designer may consider 'never emit a word that was not sent' an implicit requirement of any UART receiver. In that case this is an RTL robustness bug, not an ambiguity.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec: add a rule on receiver resynchronisation after a frame error, e.g. 'after a frame error the receiver waits for rxd=1 before detecting a new start bit', and say whether start detection is edge- or level-based. (2) If such a rule is adopted: fix RTL. Track rxd high after a frame error, e.g. add an 'wait_idle' flag set at uart_rx.v:127 and cleared when rxd_reg==1, and gate the idle-branch start at l.132 with it, or detect start on a 1->0 transition of rxd_reg. CHK-008 then stands as written. (3) If the designer decides the level-based restart is acceptable: change the test/contract stimulus, not the check strength. Either return rxd to 1 shortly after mid-stop (e.g. hold the bad stop low for about bp/2+2 cycles) so no second start is accepted, or keep the full-bit stimulus and update the reference model and contract.json:270 to expect the extra 0xFF word. Document the behaviour in the spec either way.

analyses.failure: test_regression_random — CHK-001 (Python sink checker): "m_axis stalled with tvalid=1 tdata=0x75 after tready=0 got tvalid=1 tdata=0x5b at edge 522" (sim.log:72-78)
analyses.spec_says: Same as the first analysis. spec:36-38 "Data is transferred ... only when both tvalid and tready are high, otherwise the bus is stalled." spec:42-44 "... a single cycle pulse will be emitted from overrun_error and the word is discarded." The open question at rules.json:300-301 (which word is discarded) is unanswered (rules.json:304). The contract (contract.json:181, 317) and the reference model (test l.302-304) take 'new word discarded, pending word kept'.
analyses.rtl_does: uart_rx.v:120-125: on a good stop bit the RTL loads m_axis_tdata_reg <= data_reg unconditionally (l.123) and pulses overrun_error if a word was already pending (l.125). In the regression this happens at edge 522 (about 5.2 us into the test, so the first prescale=2 pass). The pending 0x75 is replaced by 0x5b while tvalid=1 and tready=0. The SVA summary shows only one CHK-001 fail for the whole sim (sim.log:139). The regression is the last test, and the sim appears to end at the Python failure before the next rising edge where a_CHK_001 (nnc_chk_axis.sv:25-26, |=>) would evaluate. That is inferred from timing and was not confirmed in the log.
analyses.test_does: test_c_uart.py:650-731. Random sink (p_ready from {0.2,0.5,0.8,1.0}, max_wait=2*bp, l.662-664), which forces reads within 32 cycles, well under one 160-cycle frame. So overrun can only happen in the 'ov' episodes (l.682-697): wait until all words are delivered and tvalid=0, set sink 'off', send w, then after 0..bp idle send w2 with tready still 0, and model.rx_good(w2, pending=True) (l.695), i.e. the new word is discarded. The continuous AxisSink CHK-001 check (l.173-176) fires when w2's stop bit overwrites w. Expected value = the earlier tdata (0x75), derived from contract.json:181.

candidates.evidence_for: Same mechanism as test_chk_007: uart_rx.v:123 overwrites a stalled AXI output word, which conflicts with 'otherwise the bus is stalled' (spec:36-38). It reproduces in a second, independent random scenario (0x75 -> 0x5b), so it is not a one-off stimulus artefact.
candidates.evidence_against: The overrun sentence (spec:42-44) can be read as discarding the word in the tdata register (the old word), which the RTL does by design (upstream source, spec:1).

candidates.evidence_for: The reference model (l.302-304, l.315-319) and CHK-001 both hard-code the 'new word discarded' interpretation taken from contract.json:317, which the contract itself says could be read either way.
candidates.evidence_against: The stimulus is legal and matches the CHK-001 behaviour text. The episode setup (l.683-686) ensures exactly one word is pending before the overrun frame, so there is no race in the test. The checker samples correctly at falling edges (l.1-6, l.170-176).

candidates.evidence_for: The outcome depends entirely on the unanswered question at rules.json:300-301. contract.json:317 records the ambiguity.
candidates.evidence_against: The AXI stall sentence (spec:36-38) may be taken as already deciding the question in favour of the test.

analyses.options: Same root cause and decision as test_chk_007_rx_overrun; one decision resolves both. (1) Clarify which word is discarded on overrun, answering the rules.json:300 question. (2) If the pending word is kept: gate the load at uart_rx.v:123-124 on (!m_axis_tvalid_reg || m_axis_tready) and pulse overrun_error otherwise. The regression then needs no change. (3) If the old word is overwritten: update contract.json:181 and the UartRefModel. In rx_good(pending=True), replace the last expected word with the new one instead of dropping it. Add a spec-backed exception to CHK-001 for the overrun edge only, and document the AXI-stall deviation. Re-run the regression after the fix, because the failure stopped it before the CHK-005/007/008 scoreboards (l.706-731) were reached.

analyses.failure: Assertion CHK-001 (SVA a_CHK_001, verif/sva/nnc_chk_axis.sv:25-27): hits=405 fails=1, first fail 254585000 ps (sim.log:94, 139; results.json:92-96)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:181 (CHK-001, rules UA-T1.3-05 and UA-T1.3-07): "If rst=0, m_axis_tvalid=1 and m_axis_tready=0 at rising edge N ... then at rising edge N+1 m_axis_tvalid=1 and m_axis_tdata equals its value at edge N ... even if another frame finishes on rxd in the meantime (overrun discards the new word)." Source text: spec:36-38 ("otherwise the bus is stalled") and spec:42-44 ("... the word is discarded"). Which word is discarded is not stated; the question at rules.json:300-301 is still open.
analyses.rtl_does: uart_rx.v:101-103 clears tvalid only on a handshake, which is correct for normal stalls (404 of 405 stall cycles pass). uart_rx.v:120-125: when a frame's stop bit is good, l.123 writes m_axis_tdata_reg <= data_reg even if m_axis_tvalid_reg=1 and m_axis_tready=0, and l.125 raises overrun_error. The one failing evaluation is at the W2 (0xC3) stop-bit sample in test_chk_007 (fail time 254585000 ps matches sim.log:41/48), where tdata goes 0x3C -> 0xC3 under stall. COVP-016 'overrun pulse while pending word held' hit=1 (sim.log), which confirms the overrun-during-stall condition happened.
analyses.test_does: SVA: `(m_axis_tvalid && !m_axis_tready) |=> (m_axis_tvalid && $stable(m_axis_tdata))` with disable iff (rst) (nnc_chk_axis.sv:25-26). This is a direct translation of contract.json:181. The stimulus that triggered it is test_chk_007 (test_c_uart.py:452-458: tready=0, W1=0x3C pending, then W2=0xC3 received). The same check is implemented in Python at test_c_uart.py:173-176, and it also fails in test_regression_random at edge 522.

candidates.evidence_for: Standard AXI4-Stream behaviour and spec:36-38 say a stalled transfer does not change. uart_rx.v:123 has no guard on a pending word, so tdata changes under tvalid=1/tready=0. The assertion fails in exactly the overrun cycle and nowhere else (404 other stall cycles pass).
candidates.evidence_against: spec:42-44 can be read as 'the word currently in the tdata output register ... is discarded', which describes the RTL's overwrite. The RTL is the unmodified upstream design that the README spec documents (spec:1).

candidates.evidence_for: The clause '(overrun discards the new word)' in contract.json:181 rests on contract.json:317, an interpretation that the contract itself says is ambiguous. If the designer chooses the RTL reading, the property is too strong in the overrun cycle.
candidates.evidence_against: The SVA is a faithful, correctly clocked encoding of the written behaviour. It does not fire on ordinary back-pressure (404 passes), so the property itself is sound. The failing stimulus is legal.

candidates.evidence_for: The only failing cycle is the overrun cycle, and the expected value there is the subject of the open question at rules.json:300-301 (answered_questions empty, rules.json:304). contract.json:317 acknowledges both readings.
candidates.evidence_against: spec:36-38 (bus stalled unless tvalid and tready are both high) may be considered sufficient on its own to require the pending word to stay put.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec: the designer answers the rules.json:300 question and states whether the m_axis stall rule holds during overrun. (2) If the stall rule holds (pending word kept): fix RTL uart_rx.v:122-125 to load tdata/tvalid only when !m_axis_tvalid_reg || m_axis_tready, and otherwise just pulse overrun_error. a_CHK_001 stays unchanged and should then pass. (3) If overwrite is the intended behaviour: change contract.json:181 and the rule statement (rules.json:167) to describe it. Keep a_CHK_001 at full strength for every non-overrun stall cycle, and add a separate, explicit spec-backed property for the overrun cycle (e.g. at N+1 with rx_overrun_error=1, tvalid stays 1 and tdata equals the newly received word). Record the AXI-stall exception in the spec.
